### Overview

#### Definition

An event is defined as the change of status of a variable from False (=0) to True (<>0) or vice versa. The variable can be a logged channel, such as a diagnostic or an error flag, or some derived channel which has two meaningful statuses (e.g. a Boolean condition). When the variable changes status an event is generated.

Examples

  * Gear shifts are events which are generated by the change of status of the logged gear number channel.

  * Alarm events can be generated by error flags changing from false to true

  * Corner entry/exit is an event generated when lateral acceleration exceeds a certain value




Events can be displayed as markers in [Graph](../../AnalysisWnds/Wnds/GRA/GRAWndOverview.md), [XY](../../AnalysisWnds/Wnds/XY/XYWndOverview.md), [XYZ](../../AnalysisWnds/Wnds/XYZ/XYZWndOverview.md), [Track](../../AnalysisWnds/Wnds/CRV/CRVWndOverview.md) windows, as statistics in lap reports and in [event reports](../../AnalysisWnds/Wnds/EVR/EVRWndOverview.md).

Click [here](Event_setup.md) to find out about setting up events.

#### Graph windows

  * Events are displayed within or below graphic windows with markers, icons or lines . A variety of styles and options can be configured for individual event types. Default styles are setup in Tools/Events/Default Settings.

  * Tooltips on each event marker show the type and the value of event and can show the value of associated channels at the event time.




  * Individual events can be displayed in graphic windows by dragging them from the channel browser. When an event is hidden in graphs, it will still be calculated and listed in the event reports and can be searched via the Event Search function.

  * Global events are defined as an event displayed in every window. Their symbol is . This global graphic property means an automatic drag in all windows (it is true even in all new windows). A Global event can be set via mouse right click command in the Channel Browser panel or via flag in edit event page




  * Events which are active in a window are shown with a green icon in the channel browser. A yellow icon indicates that the event is not associated with the dataset displayed.

  * Use Ctrl+drag from the Channel Browser to graph the event as a virtual channel

  * All events can be hidden or displayed in individual windows by clicking on the Show Events button

  * The [Search Event](../../WTXWorkWindows/WndSearchEvents/WndSearchEvents.md) function allows to step through occurrences of one or more types of event within the data.

  * Event markers can be displayed also in the following window types: [XY](../../AnalysisWnds/Wnds/XY/XYWndOverview.md), [XYZ](../../AnalysisWnds/Wnds/XYZ/XYZWndOverview.md) and [Track](../../AnalysisWnds/Wnds/CRV/CRVWndOverview.md) window

#### Automation

Automation interfaces is extended to add [OLE](../../Automation/OLE_AUTOMATION.md) events which are triggered when events are found. These events can be caught with external applications or internal scripts. See OnEvent in Applications scripts.

#### Make Event Logs

There is a command in the [Data Browser](../../DataBrw/Menu.md) to create processed Event Logs based on a selection of data which are saved in the ZTX archive at the device level (allowing to create a report for the whole session for each vehicle). The command is "Tools / Make Event Logs". 

Event reports files are saved with EVL file extension inside the data archive. The file format is XML.

The EVL files are stored in the archive in a folder with the structure [Device]\Events\\[EventName]\ where [Device] is the Device folder, and [EventName] is the name of the single event.

Each Event Log will contain the names of the groups/events within the libraries that it was created from. They will not include the full event definitions as these are basically subsets of VCH libraries.

The Event Comment field, if present, will be used to identify the Event in WinTAX4 environment as explained below

An associated [Auto Rx task](../../Acquisition_Manager/Rx_tasks/Rx_tasks.md#MakeEventLog) will allow the Event Log to be created during the acquisition session (real time and cable download). For each following run the entries will be appended to the existing report (at device level).
